title: Copy Focus Deck Data
eyebrow: Proposal, revised while planning · 15 October 2026 · Unblock

short.lead: You want Unblock to start with a copy of Focus Deck's data, synced with the same GitHub token, so that editing the copy can never change the original. The Gist (GitHub's hosted sync file) is already safe. The risk is the GitHub issues that tasks are linked to: the copy would still point at the same real issues, so a change in Unblock would show up in Focus Deck.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it does and what it needs from you.
items: Unblock reads and writes only its own sync file, unblock-state.json, and only looks for Gists that hold that file (app/js/sync.js lines 10 and 83). It never finds or opens Focus Deck's Gist. Browser storage is kept apart too, and scripts/check-isolation-browser.mjs checks that.
A one-time copy of the Gist

A 'Copy from Focus Deck' button in Unblock's Settings. It reads Focus Deck's Gist without writing to it, then puts that data into a new private Gist that belongs to Unblock. Focus Deck's Gist is never written to.
Paste your GitHub token into Unblock once. It is the same token Focus Deck uses, but Unblock keeps its own stored copy.
Decide what happens to issue links

Some copied tasks are linked to GitHub issues. In Unblock, completing, deleting, relabelling or reprioritising one of those tasks changes the real issue (app/js/github-sync.js:112, 131, 170, 189), and Focus Deck shows that same issue.
Done: you approved cutting the links.
Unblock pulls the same issues itself

Whenever a token is saved, Unblock's own GitHub auto-sync imports every open issue that carries any label from up to 20 of your repos (app/js/github-sync.js, syncGithub, lines 549 to 582). Focus Deck pulls those same repos. So after the copy, the next auto-sync would bring the issues back as new linked tasks beside the unlinked copies, and editing those would change the real issues. Cutting the copied links is not enough on its own.
Pick an answer to the auto-sync question in the choices below.

changes: Copies Focus Deck's sync data into a new Unblock Gist.

Using your token, it finds Focus Deck's Gist, reads it, and creates a separate private Gist for Unblock. If Unblock already holds data, the copied data is merged with it instead of replacing it. Focus Deck's sync file is focus-deck-state.json (Focus Deck app/js/sync.js:10), so the copy looks for a Gist that holds that file.
Unblock starts with every Focus Deck project, task and note.
Focus Deck's Gist is only ever read.
The code that merges synced data (app/js/merge.js) does not change.
choices: issues
What should the copy do with tasks linked to GitHub issues?
A
Cut the links in the copy

Each copied task keeps its owner/repo#N reference as plain text but is no longer linked to the GitHub issue. Nothing Unblock does can change an issue that Focus Deck shows. You can re-link tasks later, when Unblock replaces Focus Deck.
B
Copy the links as they are
The Gists stay separate, but both apps use the same GitHub issues, so a change in either app shows up in the other. This only makes sense once Unblock replaces Focus Deck.
C
Add a 'GitHub read-only' switch
Unblock still pulls issues but never writes to them while the switch is on. It needs more code than cutting the links, and the shared-issue risk returns the moment the switch goes off.
Approved: cut the links.
autosync
How should Unblock stop its own auto-sync from re-linking the same issues?
A
A GitHub issues switch in Settings, off to start with

Unblock uses your token for its own sync file only, and never reads or writes issues while the switch is off. The import and every issue write check the switch. You turn it on when Unblock replaces Focus Deck, then re-link tasks.
B
Leave the copied repos out of Unblock's auto-sync

The copy adds every repo whose tasks it unlinked to Unblock's list of excluded repos. Repos the copy did not include would still sync, and Focus Deck pulls those too, so new issues there would be shared.
C
Make GitHub read-only in Unblock
Unblock still imports issues but never writes to them. The imported issues would still arrive as new tasks beside the unlinked copies, so each issue would appear twice.
I recommend the switch. It is the only answer that keeps every issue apart, and it is two checks in existing code: one where auto-sync starts and one in front of the issue writes.

wrapup.summary: A one-time copy of Focus Deck's sync data into a new Unblock Gist, using the same GitHub token, with Focus Deck's Gist only ever read.
wrapup.changing: Unblock's Settings gains a 'Copy from Focus Deck' button. Focus Deck does not change.
wrapup.blocking: Your pick for the auto-sync question. Focus Deck's sync file is focus-deck-state.json (Focus Deck app/js/sync.js:10, read from a read-only copy), so nothing else is missing.
